title: Model merging: weighted, SLERP, task arithmetic
hook: Why averaging weights can work, what ModelMergeSimple's ratio really is, and the sums behind the rule: merge unquantized files, quantize after.

verified.claim: ModelMergeSimple adds model2 with strength 1 - ratio and multiplies model1 by ratio. The real calculate_weight gave 4.4 for model1 10, model2 2, ratio 0.3, and 10 for ratio 1.
A merged weight is stored by stochastic_rounding, seeded per key, when the stored format is FP8.
No SLERP node for merging exists in core's merging files.

Task vectors are defined by subtraction in the Task Arithmetic paper, and its abstract covers negation and addition. Model soups' abstract says averaging often improves accuracy and robustness with no extra inference or memory cost.
With a mismatched shape the real calculate_weight logs the warning and adds nothing, but still multiplies the weight by strength_model: 10 became 5 at ratio 0.5.

Merging rounded parents grows the error by 1.38 in FP8 while their rounding errors are unrelated (correlation 0.006). An even grid with unrelated parents gave 1.41, and FP8 parents 1% apart gave 1.04.
verified.ref: side script on the lab's fp8 function

unchecked: The numbers use stand-in Gaussian weights and rounding to nearest. ComfyUI itself uses stochastic rounding when it stores FP8 again, which CU-212 shows costs more noise. Real weights have other distributions.
We ran no real merge and no render here. Whether a merged image model looks good is untested.
Those two papers study classifiers and language models, mostly. They say nothing about image-generation checkpoints, so 'it often helps' is not shown for them.
That lerp shrinking weights by a tiny amount harms pictures is not shown. We removed the draft's claims about grey noise, black images and washed-out output.
